_comment: Reference data for tools/masked_hint.py — correlating MASKED account-recovery hints (de*****@mail.example, *******08, +84 *** *** *12, •••• 4321) against selectors a case already holds. A hint match is CORROBORATING only: it may raise confidence in a selector that is ALREADY linked by real evidence, never create a join key, never a KB edge (CLAUDE.md RULE 5). Keys starting with _ are documentation.

mask_chars._comment: `always` are never a real selector character, so they mask in every hint. `contextual` are legal in an e-mail local part (x, _), so in an E-MAIL hint they only count as a mask when the hint has no `always` mask character and they form a run of at least `email_min_run`; in a phone/digit hint they always mask.

providers._comment: Length semantics of a mask run, per provider that DISPLAYED the hint (not the mail domain). `unknown` = the run is a display constant/padding and says nothing about how many characters it hides (match one-or-more). `exact` = one mask character per hidden character. Every major recovery flow observed pads with a fixed-width run, so all are `unknown` until an analyst verifies otherwise against an account they control — switching one to `exact` without that check silently drops true matches. `generic_exact` exists for a site whose hint was verified to be per-character.

unknown.note: default — the mask run length is not trusted

microsoft.note: fixed-width padding after the first characters of the local part; phone shows the last digits

google.note: first characters of the local part, padded run; phone shows the last digits

apple.note: first character(s) and the masked domain; phone shows the last digits

facebook.note: first and last local-part characters with a padded run; masked domain label

instagram.note: first and last local-part characters with a padded run

paypal.note: first local-part character and first domain character, padded runs

generic_exact.note: one mask character per hidden character — use only when verified

matching._comment: `min_hidden` = the fewest characters an unknown-length run may stand for. `min_visible_email` / `min_visible_phone` = discriminating visible characters a hint needs before a single unique match is reported as `corroborates` (below it the verdict is `consistent`: the hint does not contradict the candidate, but too little is shown to single it out). Visible characters of a common mail domain are not discriminating.

common_mail_domains._comment: Mail domains shared by millions of unrelated accounts: their visible letters carry no discriminating weight in a hint.

calling_codes._comment: ITU country calling codes used to split an E.164 candidate into country code + national number (stdlib only, no phonenumbers). Longest prefix wins.

case_scan._comment: How --case enumerates the selectors a case already holds (read-only). JSON files under cases/<id>/ larger than `max_file_bytes` are skipped. A string is an e-mail candidate when the whole value is an address; a phone candidate only under a key containing one of `phone_keys`.
